headline: A Ukrainian military intelligence unit says its ground robots pulled 45 soldiers out from under Russian fire over the summer.
score_reason: Raised from 5 to 7 by Rafi's order of 10 Oct 2026
importance_line: Robots are increasingly doing the most dangerous supply and evacuation runs for Ukrainian soldiers, but the numbers come only from the unit itself and it did not say how many vehicles or trips were involved.
summary: Kyiv Post reports, citing RBC-Ukraine, that the Artan special unit of Ukraine's Military Intelligence Directorate (HUR) says its remote-controlled ground robots evacuated 45 soldiers from under Russian fire, delivered more than 41 tons of supplies and drove a combined 4,258 kilometers (2,646 miles) during the summer campaign. Col. Viktor Torkotiuk, commander of the Artan unit, says the robots free up forces for active operations, and Kyiv Post adds that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has set a target of at least 50,000 ground robotic systems for the military in 2026.
notes: Source chain: Kyiv Post wrote the article and cites RBC-Ukraine for the commander's statements; all figures are the unit's own and unchecked. Figures cover summer 2026, announced 9 Oct 2026. Score 7 by Rafi's order of 10 Oct 2026.
